mechanism: A binary verification process comparing the definition hashes or schema of two entities (agents, {{artifact}}s, or protocols) to determine whether they can interact without translation. The result is directional: hash equality is mutual, but schema compatibility need not be — a reader of a later version may accept earlier data while the reverse fails.
invariants: Determinism: identical inputs always yield the same result.
Directional: the result states which entity can consume which. Mutual compatibility is a separate claim, established by checking both directions.
failure_modes: Symmetry assumed: a one-way result is read as mutual, so a producer is cleared to consume from a partner it can only send to.
